data_schema.title: USDA Directive Extraction Schema v2.1 (DR/DM)
data_schema.description: Extracts metadata and structured policy statements from 3000 series USDA Departmental Regulation (DR) or Departmental Manual (DM). Governing rules: (1) Any field described as verbatim must be copied character-for-character from the source document. Never paraphrase, merge, abbreviate, summarize, or insert ellipses. (2) Do not infer. If the source does not support an optional field, leave the field out entirely. Never return an empty string or a guess. (3) Only the label fields in policy_statements (statement_kind, statement_function, modal_use, normative_force, actor_basis) are interpretations. Every other field is quoted or copied from the document.

document_type.description: Type of document as printed in the header, such as 'Departmental Regulation' or 'Departmental Manual'.

issuing_organization.description: Organization issuing the document, verbatim from the header.

issuing_location.description: Location of the issuing organization, verbatim from the header.

regulation_number.description: Official document number from the header, verbatim, for example 'DR 3105-001'.

subject.description: Subject or title of the document, verbatim from the header.

issue_date.description: Issue date from the header, as written.

expiration_date.description: Expiration date from the header, as written. Leave out if none is printed.

opi.description: Office of Primary Interest (OPI) from the header, verbatim.

supersedes.description: The prior document this document supersedes. Take all values from the supersession paragraph in the body (usually under Special Instructions/Cancellations), NOT from the header. Leave the whole object out if the document supersedes nothing.

document_number.description: Number of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph. If it is identical to this document's own number, still copy it from the supersession paragraph, not the header.

document_title.description: Title of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph.

document_date.description: Date of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph.

scope.description: The text of the Scope section, verbatim. Do not add words. Leave out if the document has no Scope section.

purpose.description: The text of the Purpose section, verbatim. Do not add words. Leave out if the document has no Purpose section.

inquiries.description: Contact information from the Inquiries section. Leave out any property the document does not state; never return an empty string.

office.description: Office or division named for inquiries, verbatim. Leave out if the document names no office.

email.description: Email address given for inquiries, verbatim, without trailing punctuation. Leave out if none is given.

table_of_contents.description: Top-level entries of the printed table of contents, in order, including appendices. Return an empty list if the document prints no table of contents.

section_number.description: Section or appendix identifier as printed, for example '1.' or 'Appendix A'.

section_title.description: Section or appendix title as printed in the table of contents.

page.description: Page number exactly as printed in the table of contents, for example '2' or 'A-1'. Copy it even if the section actually starts on a different page. Leave out if no page number is printed.

actors.description: Registry of every distinct entity that the policy text names in an acting role. One entry per entity. Include every entity used as actor_name in policy_statements. Also include entities the document names in a role without being directed to act (mark those mentioned_only). Documents (bylaws, regulations, directives) are NEVER actors and must not appear here. Return an empty list if the document names no actors.

name.description: The entity's name exactly as written in the policy text, without a leading article ('the') and without a possessive. Keep a compound name intact if the document writes it as one phrase, for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices'. This is the join key used by actor_name in policy_statements, so spell it identically there.

components.description: ONLY for a name that joins separate entities with commas or 'and' (for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices' gives 'USDA Mission Areas', 'agencies', 'staff offices'). NEVER split a job title from the organization that qualifies it ('Director of IT, Office of the Inspector General' is ONE position), and never split an organization name from the position it modifies ('Office of the Chief Information Officer (OCIO) Associate CIOs (ACIO)' is ONE group). Each component is a verbatim substring of the name. Leave out for single entities.

items.description: One verbatim component of a compound actor name.

actor_type.description: Kind of entity. Use exactly one of: position (a job title, singular or plural, for example 'USDA CIO' or 'Mission Area Assistant CIOs'), office (an organizational unit, for example 'OCIO Executive Secretariat'), council_or_body (a council, committee, board, or similar body), group (a category of organizations or units, not job titles, for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices'), external_entity (an entity outside the document's authority), program_or_system (an IT initiative, system, program, or project that the document says must act or conform).

binding_status.description: bound_by_this_document: the document directs, permits, or assigns a function or role to this entity and has authority over it. mentioned_only: the document names the entity but cannot or does not impose anything on it (for example a council or agency outside USDA that the document says a USDA body partners with).

policy_statements.description: Structured statements from the numbered body sections only (not the table of contents, not the appendices). RULES. (a) SENTENCES: emit one statement per sentence. If a paragraph has more than one sentence, give each its own statement with ids suffixed .s1, .s2, and so on. Abbreviations and legal citations ('U.S.C.', 'CFR', '§', 'et seq.') do not end a sentence. (b) LISTS: when text introduces a list (usually ends with a colon, for example 'The USDA CIO will:'), emit the introducing text as one statement with statement_kind 'lead_in', and emit EVERY item of the list as its own statement with statement_kind 'list_item' and parent_statement_id set to the id of the lead_in. Never skip list items, including lists of legal authorities. For a list inside a list, parent_statement_id is the immediate parent. (c) NEVER merge text from different sentences, paragraphs, or list items into one statement. (d) Copy text exactly; do not summarize. (e) PRONOUNS: when a sentence's subject is a pronoun ('It', 'Its', 'They') that refers to a named actor in the preceding sentence, resolve it: set actor_name to that actor and actor_basis to resolved_from_prior_sentence. (f) DOCUMENT AS SUBJECT: when the grammatical subject is the document itself ('This DR', 'This policy', 'Nothing in this DR'), leave actor_name out; the entities the document acts on belong in target.

statement_id.description: Printed numbering path of the statement: section number, then paragraph letter, then item number in parentheses, for example '1', '3.a', '5.d.s2', '6.a(1)'. Add '.sN' only when a paragraph contains more than one sentence. Must be unique within the document.

statement_kind.description: standalone: a complete sentence that stands on its own. lead_in: text that introduces a list and is incomplete without its items. list_item: a list item that completes its lead_in.

parent_statement_id.description: Include ONLY when statement_kind is list_item: the statement_id of its immediate lead_in. For every other statement leave this field out entirely; never return an empty string.

section_number.description: Number of the section containing the statement, digits only, for example '6'.

section_title.description: Title of the section containing the statement, as shown in the table of contents, for example 'Roles and Responsibilities'.

source_text.description: VERBATIM text of this one sentence or list item exactly as printed, including trailing punctuation such as ':' or ';' and including any list-ending words such as 'and'. No paraphrase, no ellipses, no text from any other statement. For a list_item, give only the item's own text, not the lead_in.

statement_function.description: What the statement does. obligation: a required action or compliance requirement on an actor. responsibility: a standing duty or function assigned to an actor, including present-tense descriptions of what a body does. role_designation: assigns an entity to a role, for example membership or voting status. authority: names a legal source of authority or a grant of authority. scope: states what or whom the document applies to. purpose: states why the document or a body exists. definition: defines a term. condition: states a standalone triggering condition. exception: carves out an exception. savings_clause: states that the document does not displace existing authorities or delegations. effectivity: states when the document takes effect or how long it lasts. supersession: states that the document replaces another. classification_rule: states a rule that classifies something or applies a requirement when a status is met. reference: points to another document or location. inquiry: tells who may be contacted. container: use for every lead_in statement. other: none of the above.

modal_verb.description: The modal word or phrase of the statement's MAIN clause, exactly as written, for example 'will', 'can', 'may', 'must', 'shall', 'must not'. Ignore modals inside relative or subordinate clauses (for 'advises the USDA CIO on IT matters that may become IT investments', the 'may' is not the statement's modal). For a list_item whose own text has no modal, copy the modal from its lead_in. Leave out if the main clause has no modal.

modal_use.description: deontic: the main-clause modal directs, permits, or prohibits action by an actor (for example 'The Deputy CIO will serve', 'can direct questions'). predictive: the modal only states what will happen or remain true (for example 'It will remain in effect until superseded'). none: the main clause has no modal.

normative_force.description: mandatory: deontic 'will', 'shall', or 'must' directing an actor to act or to serve in a role. prohibitive: deontic 'must not', 'shall not', or 'may not'. permissive: deontic 'may' or 'can'. assigned: a present-tense statement with no deontic modal that assigns or describes a function, duty, or role of a named actor (for example 'The CIO Council advises the USDA CIO on...', 'It assesses the needs of...'); use it only when actor_name is present, and never for purpose statements. descriptive: everything else with no deontic force, including purpose, scope, supersession, effectivity, savings clauses, references, authorities, definitions, and statements about the document itself or about other documents. not_applicable: use for every lead_in; its force is carried by its list_items.

actor_name.description: The entity directed to act, permitted to act, or assigned a function or role by this statement, spelled exactly as in the matching actors[].name. It must appear in source_text or in the lead_in's text (leading article removed); for a resolved pronoun, copy it from the antecedent sentence. Leave out when the statement binds no actor: scope, supersession, effectivity, savings clauses, statements about documents (including bylaws), and any statement whose subject is the document itself ('This DR', 'This policy', 'Nothing in this DR'). Never supply an actor that is not stated in the text or resolvable from the preceding sentence. Always leave out for lead_in statements.

actor_basis.description: Include ONLY when actor_name is present; otherwise leave this field out entirely. explicit_in_statement: the actor appears in this statement's own source_text. inherited_from_lead_in: the actor appears only in the lead_in that this list_item completes. resolved_from_prior_sentence: the subject is a pronoun resolved to the actor named in the preceding sentence.

target.description: VERBATIM phrase naming what the action is directed at or what the statement applies to, starting at the first word after any leading article ('a', 'an', 'the'). For a role_designation, the body or unit the role is within (for example 'CIO Council'). Leave out if none.

resulting_status.description: VERBATIM phrase naming the status or role that a role_designation or classification_rule confers, for example 'voting member' or 'advisory (non-voting) members'. Leave out for other statements.

conditions.description: VERBATIM phrases that restrict when or to what the statement applies, for example 'that the CIO Council designates as enterprise initiatives'. Do NOT treat a non-restrictive descriptive phrase set off by commas (for example 'appointed by the USDA CIO' in 'The Secretariat, appointed by the USDA CIO, will serve') as a condition. Leave out if there are none.

items.description: One verbatim condition phrase copied from source_text.

cross_references.description: Other documents, laws, or regulations cited in source_text, each copied verbatim as ONE entry per cited authority, including its code citation (for example 'The Clinger-Cohen Act of 1996, 40 United States Code (U.S.C.) § 11101 et seq.' is one entry; for a list_item that is just a citation, the entry is the item text without the trailing ';' or 'and'). Never add a separate entry for a title that is part of the same citation (the words 'Chief Information Officer' after '7 CFR § 2.32'). Never list generic categories such as 'law' or 'Federal regulation'. Leave out if none.

acronyms.description: Acronyms and abbreviations listed in the acronym appendix, one entry per row, in order. Return an empty list if the document has no acronym appendix.

acronym.description: Acronym or abbreviation exactly as printed.

authorities_and_references.description: Entries of the Authorities and References appendix, one per entry, each copied verbatim, including any date, in order. Return an empty list if the document has no such appendix.

items.description: One appendix entry exactly as printed, joined across line breaks.

policy_statements.source_text: This Departmental Regulation (DR) establishes the policy for enterprise geospatial data management (EGDM) in the United States Department of Agriculture (USDA).
Led by the Office of the Chief Information Officer (OCIO), this DR defines the strategic direction necessary to optimize the management of the USDA geospatial data and geospatial infrastructure.
policy_statements.target: USDA geospatial data and geospatial infrastructure

policy_statements.source_text: The USDA EGDM policy will help to achieve the requirements of:
The Geospatial Data Act (GDA) of 2018 (43 United States Code (U.S.C.) Ch. 46, Geospatial Data);
cross_references: The Geospatial Data Act (GDA) of 2018 (43 United States Code (U.S.C.) Ch. 46, Geospatial Data)

policy_statements.source_text: The National Spatial Data Infrastructure [NSDI] Strategic Plan 2021-2024; and
cross_references: The National Spatial Data Infrastructure [NSDI] Strategic Plan 2021-2024

policy_statements.source_text: Office of Management and Budget (OMB) Circular A-16, Coordination of Geographic Information and Related Spatial Data Activities.
cross_references: Office of Management and Budget (OMB) Circular A-16, Coordination of Geographic Information and Related Spatial Data Activities

policy_statements.source_text: This EGDM DR establishes the policy framework to implement GDA and NSDI guidance.

Many of the policy elements also reflect Mission Area, agency, staff office, executive, and geospatial program management requirements, as well as demonstrate an enterprisewide public service enhancement.
This policy creates consolidated Departmental direction for Mission Area, agency, and staff office management of geospatial data.
policy_statements.target: Mission Area, agency, and staff office management of geospatial data

policy_statements.source_text: It is consistent with Departmental policies and delegations of authority.
This DR helps ensure coordinated action and responsiveness within the Department, and between external stakeholders, on EGDM issues.

This DR applies to all USDA Mission Areas, agencies, staff offices, programs, teams, organizations, appointees, and employees, including contractors and grantees receiving Federal funds that utilize and collect geospatial data.
policy_statements.target: USDA Mission Areas, agencies, staff offices, programs, teams, organizations, appointees, and employees, including contractors and grantees receiving Federal funds that utilize and collect geospatial data
conditions: that utilize and collect geospatial data

policy_statements.source_text: This policy introduces the geospatial data management objectives for the implementation of the GDA for the adoption of geospatial data management best practices, used by USDA internal and external geospatial data creators, partners, publishers, and consumers.

This DR applies to USDA’s geospatial portfolio, including all geospatial data created for, by, and enhanced by USDA, with a priority focus on the USDA’s National Geospatial Data Assets (NGDA), other data supporting NGDA data theme communities and NSDI, and other Geospatial Authoritative Data (GAD).
GAD is any geospatial data that meets one or more of the following:
Is defined by statute;
Is authored, maintained, and considered authoritative by USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices;
Is used to support policy;
Is used to manage programs; or
Is used to inform the public.
The USDA geospatial data will include geospatial standards processes to ensure data integrity throughout the lifecycle, including the acquisition, storage, and distribution process.
Authoritative data products used in emergency response situations will have established data lifecycle controls before and after emergency deployments.
policy_statements.target: Authoritative data products used in emergency response situations

policy_statements.source_text: During emergency response execution, the USDA Geospatial Information Officer (GIO) will defer to Mission Area, agency, and staff office discretion in the determination of the characteristics of authoritative data products.
policy_statements.target: Mission Area, agency, and staff office discretion in the determination of the characteristics of authoritative data products

policy_statements.source_text: This DR supersedes DR 3465-001, Enterprise Geospatial Data Management, dated August 5, 2016.
cross_references: DR 3465-001, Enterprise Geospatial Data Management, dated August 5, 2016

policy_statements.source_text: This DR is effective immediately when published.
All Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices that utilize and collect geospatial data will align their policies and procedures with this DR within 6 months of its publication.
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices
conditions: that utilize and collect geospatial data

policy_statements.source_text: All Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices that utilize and collect geospatial data will develop a 5-year road map for geospatial program implementation within 1 year of DR publication.
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices
conditions: that utilize and collect geospatial data

policy_statements.source_text: USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices use geospatial data to ensure evidence-based procedures, ensure continuity of operations, make decisions, and inform policies.
policy_statements.actor_name: USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices

policy_statements.source_text: Geospatial applications support the delivery of all key USDA programs including trade, emergency response, farm loans, conservation, research, forestry, fire, and pandemic response.
In 2018, the GDA was signed into law.
The Act was designed to ensure that our Nation invests and utilizes geospatial data effectively and efficiently, and to support the NSDI.
The Act describes some of the required geospatial data management efforts, such as:
Metadata and data lifecycle management to ensure that data can be found and used effectively;
To promote data sharing efforts to reduce redundancy and decrease costs;
To promote the use of geospatial data for improved management and decision making; and
To appropriately resource geospatial data.

The EGDM policy supports the implementation of the GDA and delegates geospatial executive authority; establishes geospatial data asset management responsibility; directs participation on statutory, national advisory, and interagency committees; and prescribes procedures governing the USDA geospatial portfolio.
The USDA GIO serves as the Senior Agency Official for Geospatial Information (SAOGI) for USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices with major programmatic geospatial responsibilities.
policy_statements.target: USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices
policy_statements.resulting_status: Senior Agency Official for Geospatial Information (SAOGI)

policy_statements.source_text: The USDA GIO leads the Enterprise Geospatial Management Office (EGMO), a component of the OCIO, and provides management oversight for USDA’s geospatial portfolio.

In concert with the EGMO’s Geospatial Change Control Board (GCCB; “the Board”), or a similar EGMO organization that ensures representation of all its Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices with a geospatial portfolio, the USDA GIO will prepare, maintain, publish, and implement a geospatial strategic plan for advancing geographic information, related geospatial data, and activities in support of:
The USDA Strategic Plan Fiscal Years 2022-2026;
cross_references: The USDA Strategic Plan Fiscal Years 2022-2026

policy_statements.source_text: The USDA Information Technology Strategic Plan FY 2022-2026; and
cross_references: The USDA Information Technology Strategic Plan FY 2022-2026

policy_statements.source_text: The National Spatial Data Infrastructure Strategic Plan 2021-2024.
cross_references: The National Spatial Data Infrastructure Strategic Plan 2021-2024

policy_statements.source_text: The USDA Geospatial Strategic Plan will be reviewed by the USDA GIO and members of the GCCB annually and updated thereafter as required;

USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices that utilize and collect geospatial data will establish processes and infrastructure necessary to maintain, disseminate, preserve, and identify authoritative geospatial data;
policy_statements.actor_name: USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices
conditions: that utilize and collect geospatial data

policy_statements.source_text: The USDA EGMO and each USDA Mission Area, agency, and staff office that utilize and collect geospatial data will integrate geospatial data from all sources through collaboration, system architecture, infrastructure, and communications.
policy_statements.actor_name: USDA EGMO and each USDA Mission Area, agency, and staff office
conditions: that utilize and collect geospatial data

policy_statements.source_text: This DR is consistent with the aims of the Modernizing Government Technology Act of 2017 (MGT Act).
cross_references: Modernizing Government Technology Act of 2017 (MGT Act)

policy_statements.source_text: The MGT Act was enacted as part of the National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA) for Fiscal Year 2018 on December 12, 2017 (Subtitle G, Modernizing Government Technology, §§ 1076-1078).
cross_references: National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA) for Fiscal Year 2018

policy_statements.source_text: The MGT Act authorizes two types of funds for the purpose of modernizing the Federal Government’s legacy information technology (IT), and to incentivize IT savings in Federal agencies.

USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices responsible for GAD creation and maintenance will ensure that official records and other GAD are included on Mission Area, agency, and staff office record schedules approved by the National Archives and Records Administration per DR 3080-001, Records Management;
policy_statements.actor_name: USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices
conditions: responsible for GAD creation and maintenance

policy_statements.source_text: USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices will fulfill the responsibilities of effective geospatial data collection, product development, and data stewardship activities, and support the activities of the Federal Geographic Data Committee (FGDC), at EGMO’s request;
policy_statements.actor_name: USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices
policy_statements.target: effective geospatial data collection, product development, and data stewardship activities

policy_statements.source_text: USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices will:
Use FGDC-endorsed geospatial data standards per the GDA, and as stated on the FGDC Geospatial Standards website;
policy_statements.actor_name: USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices

policy_statements.source_text: Where available, create geospatial metadata, compliant with FGDC-endorsed standards, per FGDC-STD-001-1998, Content Standard for Digital Geospatial Metadata;
policy_statements.actor_name: USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices
cross_references: FGDC-STD-001-1998, Content Standard for Digital Geospatial Metadata

policy_statements.source_text: For all geospatial data, follow USDA-specific requirements for metadata content, to include future Departmental Manuals (DM) and guidelines;
policy_statements.actor_name: USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices

policy_statements.source_text: Ensure metadata is certified and documented; and
policy_statements.actor_name: USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices

policy_statements.source_text: Make the metadata available through the FGDC’s GeoPlatform, unless legally restricted;
policy_statements.actor_name: USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices

policy_statements.source_text: USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices will coordinate and work in partnership with other Federal, state, tribal, and local governments; higher education; and the private sector to efficiently and cost-effectively collect, integrate, maintain, disseminate, and preserve geospatial data.
policy_statements.actor_name: USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices
policy_statements.target: other Federal, state, tribal, and local governments; higher education; and the private sector

policy_statements.source_text: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices will coordinate data acquisition and management to limit duplicative or redundant activities to maximize the efficiency and collaboration in Departmental management of geospatial data, building upon existing non-Federal geospatial data to the extent possible.
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices

policy_statements.source_text: USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices will use geospatial information and services to support decision making, enhance operations, communicate with the public, and enhance reporting to Congress and the public;
policy_statements.actor_name: USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices

policy_statements.source_text: When creating and using geospatial data that contains personally identifiable information (PII), USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices will follow PII guidelines, per DR 3515-002, Privacy Policy and Compliance for Personally Identifiable Information (PII);
policy_statements.actor_name: USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices
conditions: When creating and using geospatial data that contains personally identifiable information (PII)
cross_references: DR 3515-002, Privacy Policy and Compliance for Personally Identifiable Information (PII)

policy_statements.source_text: USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices will participate in determining whether declassified data can contribute to and become part of the NSDI, in support of:
DR 3440-001, USDA Classified National Security Information Program;
cross_references: DR 3440-001, USDA Classified National Security Information Program

policy_statements.source_text: DR 3440-002, Control and Protection of “Sensitive Security Information”; and
cross_references: DR 3440-002, Control and Protection of “Sensitive Security Information”

policy_statements.source_text: DR 3440-003, Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) Program.

Prior to expending funds for geospatial data collection, USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices will search all sources, including the FGDC’s GeoPlatform and its Marketplace, to determine whether data and associated acquisition suitable for the intended purpose exists;
policy_statements.actor_name: USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices
conditions: Prior to expending funds for geospatial data collection

policy_statements.source_text: USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices will ensure that contracts, grants, agreements, and business processes are written to ensure that geospatial data collected utilizing Federal funds is high quality and meets the business requirements;
policy_statements.actor_name: USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices
policy_statements.target: contracts, grants, agreements, and business processes

policy_statements.source_text: The USDA GIO (or appointed delegates) will act as the contact to coordinate with the lead covered agencies for collection, acquisition, maintenance, and dissemination of NGDA data themes used by the USDA and will coordinate and manage the annual lead covered agency reporting effort; and

The USDA GIO (or appointed delegates) will coordinate and manage the annual GDA covered agency reporting requirements and responses to the biannual covered agency Office of the Inspector General (OIG) investigation.
policy_statements.target: annual GDA covered agency reporting requirements and responses to the biannual covered agency Office of the Inspector General (OIG) investigation

policy_statements.source_text: The USDA Chief Information Officer (CIO) will:
Delegate executive leadership for geospatial technology, data, and information solutions to the USDA GIO;
Approve revisions to the USDA Geospatial Strategic Plan;
Review and approve policy waiver or exception requests.
As the owner of this DR, the CIO will have the final review and approval authority for any waiver or exception requests;
Ensure appropriate procedural DMs are written to provide specific guidance for this DR; and
Approve DMs written to provide specific guidance to this DR.
The USDA GIO will:

Serve as the SAOGI, the senior executive responsible for Departmental geospatial strategy, planning, coordination, assessment, and synchronization of all USDA geospatial data activities, assigned to the GIO per OMB A-16 requirements;
Have authority, responsibility, and coordination for USDA’s geospatial information technology portfolio;

Oversee and facilitate the USDA internal external and implementation of the geospatial IT and geospatial data policies, governance, directives, requirements, management, product, and service standardization;
policy_statements.target: geospatial IT and geospatial data policies, governance, directives, requirements, management, product, and service standardization

policy_statements.source_text: Review and ensure procedural DMs are written to provide specific guidance for this DR.
These will be approved by the CIO prior to publication;
Serve as the policy-level official representing USDA at the FGDC;
Appoint Mission Area, agency, and staff office representatives to serve on FGDC coordination groups, governance, and working groups;
policy_statements.target: Mission Area, agency, and staff office representatives

policy_statements.source_text: Serve as GCCB Executive Champion for the activities of the GCCB;
In collaboration with the GCCB, annually review the USDA Geospatial Strategic Plan, and update it at least every 5 years, as warranted;

Maintain a knowledge base of USDA geospatial portfolio investments, oversee the enterprise geospatial capital planning process per DR 3130-013, Information Technology Capital Planning and Investment Control, and the investment control process per DR 3130-010, United States Department of Agriculture Enterprise Information Technology Governance, and advocate for Mission Area, agency, and staff office geospatial portfolio budgets and acquisition plans;
cross_references: DR 3130-013, Information Technology Capital Planning and Investment Control
DR 3130-010, United States Department of Agriculture Enterprise Information Technology Governance

policy_statements.source_text: Advocate for the use, value, and benefits of geospatial innovation and information supporting decision makers, citizens, partners, and others;
policy_statements.target: use, value, and benefits of geospatial innovation and information

policy_statements.source_text: Collaborate with the CIO, the EGMO Program Manager, the USDA Chief Data Officer, and other OCIO components to implement strategic initiatives;
policy_statements.target: CIO, the EGMO Program Manager, the USDA Chief Data Officer, and other OCIO components

policy_statements.source_text: Provide the Departmental response to external geospatial portfolio data calls;

Coordinate with the lead covered agencies for collection, acquisition, maintenance, and dissemination of NGDA data themes used by the USDA and coordinate and manage the annual lead covered agency reporting effort;
Coordinate and manage the annual FGDC GDA Covered Agency Annual Report, and other reporting requirements and responses to the biannual covered agency OIG investigation;
policy_statements.target: annual FGDC GDA Covered Agency Annual Report
cross_references: FGDC GDA Covered Agency Annual Report

policy_statements.source_text: Review and provide a recommendation to the CIO on any submitted and completed waivers to the primary requesting office for any requirement that is not in compliance with this policy.
conditions: that is not in compliance with this policy

policy_statements.source_text: The CIO, as the policy owner, will make the final decision;

extract_result.purpose:
a. This Departmental Regulation (DR) establishes the policy for enterprise geospatial data management (EGDM) in the United States Department of Agriculture (USDA). Led by the Office of the Chief Information Officer (OCIO), this DR defines the strategic direction necessary to optimize the management of the USDA geospatial data and geospatial infrastructure. The USDA EGDM policy will help to achieve the requirements of:
(1) The Geospatial Data Act (GDA) of 2018 (43 United States Code (U.S.C.) Ch. 46, Geospatial Data);
(2) The National Spatial Data Infrastructure [NSDI] Strategic Plan 2021-2024; and
(3) Office of Management and Budget (OMB) Circular A-16, Coordination of Geographic Information and Related Spatial Data Activities.
b. This EGDM DR establishes the policy framework to implement GDA and NSDI guidance. Many of the policy elements also reflect Mission Area, agency, staff office, executive, and geospatial program management requirements, as well as demonstrate an enterprisewide public service enhancement.
c. This policy creates consolidated Departmental direction for Mission Area, agency, and staff office management of geospatial data. It is consistent with Departmental policies and delegations of authority. This DR helps ensure coordinated action and responsiveness within the Department, and between external stakeholders, on EGDM issues.

a. This Departmental Regulation (DR) establishes the policy for enterprise geospatial data management (EGDM) in the United States Department of Agriculture (USDA). Led by the Office of the Chief Information Officer (OCIO), this DR defines the strategic direction necessary to optimize the management of the USDA geospatial data and geospatial infrastructure. The USDA EGDM policy will help to achieve the requirements of:

a. This DR applies to all USDA Mission Areas, agencies, staff offices, programs, teams, organizations, appointees, and employees, including contractors and grantees receiving Federal funds that utilize and collect geospatial data. This policy introduces the geospatial data management objectives for the implementation of the GDA for the adoption of geospatial data management best practices, used by USDA internal and external geospatial data creators, partners, publishers, and consumers.
